description:
Recruitment Round Overview

The Cancer Research UK Manchester Institute (CRUK MI) has opened its 2027 PhD student intake, with applications running until Friday 6 November at 17:00 GMT. Successful candidates join one of the Institute's research groups in autumn 2027 and register for their doctorate through the University of Manchester, combining institute-level cancer research with university doctoral training.

For context, we already list three of the individual CRUK MI projects on NextApply - Chromatin Regulation, Stem Cell Biology and Leukaemia Biology - each with its own page and the same deadline. The recruitment page on this entry is the parent listing that gathers the full set of projects in one place and hosts the central application route, so it is the safest single link if you want to browse every option before committing to one project.

How to Apply

Applications go through the Institute's online studentship application form - the submit-a-studentship-application route linked on the recruitment page. Prepare an academic CV, degree transcripts, two academic references and a statement explaining your fit with cancer research. Because individual projects close on the same central deadline, shortlist two or three projects in case your first choice fills.

About CRUK Manchester Institute

The Cancer Research UK Manchester Institute is one of Europe's leading cancer research centres, partnered with The University of Manchester and based partly at the Alderley Park campus. Its doctoral students work inside translational research groups spanning drug discovery, tumour biology, radiotherapy physics and precision medicine, with lab capacity and funding that few UK institutes can match.
